map.本对照表对比明式与清式古典家具在用材、造型、结构（榫卯）与纹饰上的差异，供鉴赏、: This table compares Ming-style and Qing-style classical furniture in terms of material, shape, structure (mortise and tenon) and ornament, for reference in appreciation, dating and authentication. Conclusions must combine the object with its patina and technique, and are for reference and learning only.
map.明式以黄花梨、紫檀、鸡翅木等硬木为主，讲究本色；清式偏好紫檀、红木，色泽深沉。材: Ming style mainly uses hardwoods such as huanghuali, zitan and chicken-wing wood, and values the natural color; Qing style prefers zitan and hongmu with a deep, dark tone. Grain, scent and density are the basis for judgment.
map.明式线条简练，比例优美，\"简、线、精、雅\"；清式体量厚重，雕饰繁缛，\"繁、: Ming style has concise lines and graceful proportions, "simple, linear, refined, elegant"; Qing style has heavy massing and elaborate carving, "elaborate, carved, refined, beautiful". Shape proportions are the key to dating.
map.榫卯结构是核心(不用钉子)。明式榫卯精巧隐形；看接口处理、线脚工艺、打磨光洁度。: The mortise and tenon structure is the core (no nails). Ming-style joinery is fine and concealed; observe joint treatment, molding technique and polishing smoothness. Qing-style carving is complex, combining openwork and relief.
map.明式纹饰少而精，偶有浮雕；清式纹饰繁密，常见龙凤、云纹、蝙蝠、缠枝莲等吉祥图案。: Ming-style ornament is sparse and refined, occasionally with relief; Qing-style ornament is dense, commonly featuring auspicious motifs such as dragon and phoenix, cloud, bat and interlocking lotus.
map.老家具表面有自然包浆(岁月形成的氧化层)，温润含蓄；做旧包浆浮于表面，不自然。本: Old furniture has a natural patina on the surface (an oxidation layer formed by the years), warm and understated; faked patina floats on the surface and looks unnatural. This table is for reference and learning.

map.以\"线条+用材\"区分明式与清式: Distinguishing Ming style from Qing style by "lines + material"
map.明式家具以黄花梨为主，线条简练流畅、比例舒展、装饰克制，强调结构性美（如四出头官: Ming-style furniture is mainly huanghuali, with concise flowing lines, relaxed proportions, restrained decoration and an emphasis on structural beauty (such as the four-posted official's hat armchair); Qing-style furniture is mostly zitan, with heavy material, elaborate carving, and a fondness for inlaid jade and enamel. A plain huanghuali horseshoe chair can basically be assigned to the Ming style, while a fully carved zitan throne is usually mid-to-late Qing.
map.古典家具的榫卯结构对鉴定为何重要？: Why is the mortise and tenon structure important for identification?
map.传统硬木家具以榫卯连接、少钉少胶，明式尤其讲究\"结构即装饰\"。观察榫头做法、: Traditional hardwood furniture uses mortise and tenon joinery, with few nails and little glue, and the Ming style especially emphasizes "structure as decoration". Observing how the tenon is made, and whether there are modern iron nails or chemical glue, is an important basis for judging the date and whether the piece has been repaired; spliced tenons and nailed patches are often signs of later restoration.
map.如何初步判断家具是否为老料新做？: How can you preliminarily judge whether furniture is newly made from old material?
map.老料新做指用旧木料重制新器。可看包浆是否自然连贯、磨损是否人为做旧、结构与纹饰是: Newly made from old material means remaking a new piece from reclaimed old wood. You can look at whether the patina is natural and continuous, whether the wear is artificially distressed, and whether the structure and ornament match the techniques of the period. Newly made pieces often have uniform, stiff artificial distressing that differs clearly from natural transmitted patina.
